SymbolicEssence.ArchetypalFunction: To embody mortal lifespan, human fragility, and the western boundary; father of Prometheus and mortal-oriented titans.
SymbolicEssence.SymbolicCore: The pillar between divine and mortal, progenitor of humanity's advocates.

MythicAppearances: Father of Prometheus, Epimetheus, Atlas, Menoetius
CulturalContext.ReligiousOrRitualUse: Limited direct worship; honored as western pillar; significant through his sons who championed humanity.
CulturalContext.HistoricalEvolution: Possible etymological link to Japheth (biblical); name may mean 'piercer' or relate to mortality and wounding.

SymbolicRepresentation.ImageryNotes: Rarely depicted; when shown, appears as stern titan of the west, father to humanity's greatest advocates and punished rebels.
SymbolicRepresentation.PoeticInvocation: Pillar of the west, father of the fire-bringer, who stands where immortal gives way to mortal.
SymbolicRepresentation.DreamForm: A weathered giant standing at the edge of the world where the sun sets, marking the boundary between eternal and temporal

MetaIntegration.RitualFunction: Invoked for acceptance of mortality, understanding of limits, and honoring of human advocates.
AIPromptSeeds: The father whose sons championed humanity despite the cost.
The western pillar who marks the boundary between divine and mortal realms.
NarrativeHooks: The parent whose children surpass them
